To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the configurations of high governance, education, level of wealth, and affluent level of health system are usually sufficient to explain a high life expectancy, and the configurations of low governance and health system, low level of education, and high level of wealth or low level of wealth and high level of education are usually sufficient to cause a low life expectancy.

high life expectancy is usually associated with a configuration of conditions that include high level of governance and education, wealth, health system, and low income inequality, while the opposite conditions are usually associated with low life expectancy.

high level of governance (good government), high level of education (good education), high level of wealth (good economy), and affluent health system (good health) were usually sufficient to cause high life expectancy.

the configurational effects and the causal complexity of the structural conditions on the health status of the population.
the configurational effects and the causal complexity of the macro-level structural determinants of health.
the configuration of conditions, which is an issue that is outside the scope of variable-oriented approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CSDH recommendations are usually sufficient for a high level of life expectancy.
a combination of the five structural conditions can explain life expectancy at birth better than any single condition.
high life expectancy is usually achieved by a configuration of high level of country wealth (or high level of country governance), high level of education, and high quality of health system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination of high quality governance, education, country wealth, and affluent public health system is usually sufficient to cause high life expectancy.
, in order to improve health, a high level of governance and education, a wealthy country, and an affluent health system are required.
the more a country has the structural conditions in a particular configuration, the better its health status would be.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a configuration of conditions is needed to explain health outcomes.
the configuration approach may provide a new way of thinking about the complex relations between health and social determinants of health.
it may be useful to think about the conditions for good health as a configuration rather than a single variable.
